title: Impact of Escalating Tensions and Intensified Fighting in Middle East on Singapore
what_it_is: Impact of Escalating Tensions and Intensified Fighting in Middle East on Singapore

sections.label: Singapore supports Gaza ceasefire proposal
sections.summary: Singapore supports the US ceasefire proposal codified by UN Security Council Resolution, calling for immediate ceasefire, hostage release and humanitarian access.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore firmly supports the ceasefire proposal announced by the United States (US) on 31 May 2024 which was welcomed, in fact codified, by the United Nations (UN) Security Council Resolution on 10 June 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: As the humanitarian crisis in Gaza deepens, Singapore continues to stand with the international community in calling for an immediate ceasefire, we call for the unconditional and safe release of all hostages and we also call for unhindered humanitarian access.

sections.label: Lebanon UN Resolution 1701 implementation
sections.summary: Singapore urges all parties to fully implement UN Security Council Resolution 1701 on Lebanon, including cessation of hostilities and a demilitarised zone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: With respect to Lebanon, we urge all parties to fully implement UN Security Council Resolution 1701, which inter alia called for the full cessation of hostilities and the establishment of a demilitarised zone in the south of Lebanon, permitting only the UN and Lebanese armed forces.

sections.label: Israeli settlements illegal under international law
sections.summary: Singapore views the Israeli settlements as illegal under international law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore views the Israeli settlements as illegal under international law.

sections.label: Travel advisories and Singaporean in Lebanon
sections.summary: MFA has travel advisories against Lebanon and border areas, but one Singaporean is e-registered in Lebanon and insisted on the trip.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) has existing travel advisories against travel to Lebanon and, in particular, the Israel-Lebanon border, as well as the Israel-Syria border.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I have to inform the House that there is, in fact, one Singaporean currently e-registered in Lebanon, who has insisted on proceeding with the trip despite knowing the dangers.

sections.label: Singaporeans raised $17 million assistance
sections.summary: Singaporeans of all races, languages and religions have raised more than $17 million, delivered with partners across the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: You would also recall that so far, Singaporeans have raised more than $17 million of assistance – and these funds have come from Singaporeans of all races, languages and religions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have been able to work with our partners across the Middle East to deliver this assistance.

sections.label: MFA unaware of non-e-registered Singaporeans
sections.summary: MFA will not know Singaporeans who have not e-registered, has several in Israel, and signals through advisories not to go to hotspots.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: By definition, MFA will not be aware of Singaporeans in the region who have not e-registered with us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have several in Israel – I do not have the exact number.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I want to be quite categorical – frankly, as far as MFA is concerned, it is not a matter of how strict.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have signalled unambiguously through our travel advisories and notices, "Please don't go to hotspots where safety will be an issue" or where we anticipate that further regional conflagration is a real and present risk.

sections.label: Singapore position on Gaza suffering
sections.summary: Singaporeans identify with Palestinians and are appalled by suffering in Gaza and by Hamas attacks on 7 October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Like people elsewhere in the world, Singaporeans identify with the plight of Palestinian people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But, in fact, all Singaporeans are appalled by the human suffering in Gaza as Israeli attacks target there, as they were also appalled by Hamas terrorist attacks on Israeli civilians on 7 October 2023 that prompted this IDF military operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Government has to take a national position that upholds our consistent principles and, which considers the sentiments and feelings of our population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We feel sympathy for the civilian victims on both sides and will extend humanitarian help to those in need.

sections.label: Singapore's limited role in conflict
sections.summary: Singapore has access and is heard politely, but its role is very limited until the warring leaders choose peace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, you will know that, yes, we do have access and yes, they do listen politely to us, because we have got long-standing relations and they know we do not grandstand and we do not engage in point-seeking and we are not engaged in a publicity exercise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I think you would also agree, from your trip with me, that there is a very, very limited role for us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: They are not short of advice and they are not actually short of venues to meet or avenues of communication.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But until the top leaders in the two warring tribes can arrive at a conclusion that violence is not the answer and that concessions are essential, and that these two related people have to learn to live with each other.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is that realisation and that change in spirit and perspective that will be necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, I think as far as Singapore is concerned, we stay united, we help where we can, we uphold principles and we insist on adherence to international law on all sides.
